# Invitation to co-create : AI-Dev Engineer (AI Orchestrator, Not Coder)

This year how software is built is changing fundamentally. What once required large teams, long cycles, and layers of management can now be done by a few people with good architecture, process and smart AI management.

That is how we are building at The Coherence Company \- building AI for collective intelligence, following the leading edge of AI engineering. Taking software development best practices to create professional team power in a start-up.

**To start: 1–2 month build sprint**

We are looking for our first tech team member to work hand-in-hand with the founder, creating an AI software development pipeline to build our beta product. Using AI from specification through implementation, testing, and production systems care.

The invitation is to together learn and deploy an AI-at-core software development engineering team.

### **What this role actually is (and isn’t)**

* ❌ You will **not** be writing code  
* ❌ This is **not** a traditional full-stack or backend coding role  
* ✅ You will co-design specs with the founder & AI  
* ✅ You will **supervise AI to write specs, code, test and monitor**  
* ✅ You will **research technologies and approaches for AI in the process and AI in the product** 

This is engineering as AI orchestration \- humans focus on the things AI can’t do \- vision, judgement, decision making, responsibility.

## What we are building

The first product of The Coherence Company are coherence conversations \- a new AI-in-the-loop online event system where people talk one-on-one, these conversations are recorded, published and synthesised by AI for match-making and generating collective intelligence. 

The goal is to create an experience which is deeply human yet AI powered. The AI becomes invisible.

### Coherence Conversations \- Question-centric Web conversation UI (70% beta ready)

A WebRTC conversation UI \- this is fundamentally built but needs UI polishing and testing.

#### Stack

* React  
* Deploy: Cloudflare cloud \- RealtimeKit, PartyKit, Pages

### IRIS \- Social Media generation & publishing (framework 20% complete)

An engine to take recordings, process them by creating cover images, descriptions, titles, social media posts, etc.

#### Stack

* Python/Django  
* AI synthesis through LLMs  
* Deploy: Own server, Linux/postgres

### CoCo \- AI Agent for engagement (10% complete)

An AI agent to bring people through the Coherence Conversations event experience, answering questions, inviting to conversation and engagement. 

#### Stack

* Python/Django  
* AI \- TBD  
* Deploy: Own server, Linux/postgres

### AI synthesis and matchmaking engine (research phase)

This is a key part which needs research \- for each event we need to build a memory and ability to match-make and synthesise based on the conversations within that event.

#### Stack

* Python/Django  
* ***AI memory, RAG stack \- key point of research needed***

## What matters most

**1\. Product sensitivity**  
This is not just about technical correctness. It is also about whether the thing feels clear, simple, and humane. We care about users. We want someone who can think not only about whether a system functions, but whether it makes sense in the hands of the people using it.

**2\. AI-native engineering**  
A large part of the craft here is learning how to work well with tools like Claude and other coding agents. Not casually, but seriously. Prompting well, structuring well, iterating well. Understanding that the quality of the specification shapes the quality of the implementation.

**3\. Verification mindset**  
AI can move quickly. That only matters if someone is willing to slow down where it counts. You should be the kind of person who tests carefully, checks assumptions, explores edge cases, and is willing to spend real time verifying that what was produced actually works.

**4\. Research instinct around AI systems**  
You should be curious and thoughtful about the technologies behind AI synthesis itself. Which patterns are worth using, which are wasteful, which models belong where, and how to design systems that are not just powerful but economically sane. Token costs are not a footnote. They are part of the architecture.

**5\. Systems understanding**  
You need to be able to see the whole machine. Backend architecture, Cloud, APIs, databases, service flows, system dependencies. You do not need to hand-code every layer, but you do need to understand the architecture of the whole stack and have the judgment to see where things are sound, where they are brittle, and where they are quietly going off the rails.

**6\. DevOps & infrastructure literacy**  
This role needs someone who is comfortable close to the ground. Cloud systems, debugging, monitoring, Linux, command line, keeping things running when reality refuses to match the diagram. Not glamorous, very real.

## Two possible paths

There are two ways this collaboration could work.

One path is for a **senior** who can take wide responsibility, make the process work, and contribute not only at the technical level but also through strong judgment on process, technology and product questions as the beta takes shape.

The other path is for someone a **junior** wanting to learn rapidly this new way of software development. Someone with strong curiosity, discipline, who wants to learn quickly and be coached closely by the founder.

In either case what matters most is the ability to experiment, learn fast, think clearly, verify work carefully.

### **First Engagement**

* **Project Duration:** 2 month focused sprint  
* **Commitment:** Full-time ideal, half-time possible  
* **Structure:** Direct collaboration with founder  
* **Environment:** Fast, ambiguous, minimal process overhead

We already have a clear product direction, the first software components and technology frameworks are in place, now we move to a wide beta. 

If there is a good relationship and strong alignment, as we fundraise this will grow into a long-term role in founding this company.
